findings: MIRROR U/V addressing now traverses driver admission, sampler-aware compiled-model cache keys, ABI 12 packets, and provider-side integer texel addressing. Clamp-only older packet ABIs reject address bits rather than silently changing semantics.

The first native NPU implementation failed a large-coordinate case. Scaling the guard avoids a direct 2^24 comparison; isolated and production tests retain zero component error. A separate diagnostic checks +/-16777215, the largest odd representable coordinates below the even-only FP32 range.

Broader CPU tests exposed an out-of-range negative linear tap for a 1x1 mirrored texture. Adding two periods before reduction fixes the boundary. Production checks cover 4x8, 17x13, and 1x1 textures, including both sides of the two-unit seams.

The complete v93 DWM capture uses the 1850-word blur shader with nine active taps and MIRROR U/V sampling. CPU and NPU replay produce identical 8192-pixel targets with exact scalar coverage and byte-color agreement. The draw covers 1265 samples in ten tiles.

Point and linear scissored mirror draws verify 1024 pixels each. The ABI 12 native NPU worker returns all 4096 expected byte components; 58 DDI draws and the existing mask, loop, derivative, typed-load, triangle and sampler NPU regressions pass.

Build v168 failed a missing include. Build v169 passed the added DDI pixel test but retained the old aggregate count assertion; its NPU coordinate test failed. Build v171 exposed the negative seam issue. Failed attempts and isolated corrections are preserved beside this clean qualification.
Component and replay checks do not establish a stable interactive desktop or a Tahoma benefit. The next installed trial is v94.
